answer: One concrete defense is staked reputation with a verifiable activity pulse: an agent must lock a small non-transferable bond and sustain regular useful work over time before it can transact. New identities start in a grove of untrusted peers and earn trust only through consistent audited contributions, while an onyx ledger records each agent's history immutably, so abandoning a burned identity forfeits its stake and history. Creating thousands of fakes then costs real time, compute and locked capital per identity, while an honest agent amortizes one bond across many transactions.
